Deque.name: size
Deque.documentation:
Returns the number of stored elements as int. This readonly property takes no arguments. Assignment is rejected. The receiver is unchanged. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 1.

Ownership: The receiver is borrowed readonly.

Deque.name: pushFront
Deque.documentation:
Inserts one value before the current first element. Exactly one value of the declared element type is required. Returns void and increases size by one. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushFront(2);console.log(values.popFront()!);}
```

Expected output: 2.

Ownership: Owned values transfer into the queue; scalar values copy. Borrowed payloads retain their original owners. The receiver must allow mutation.

Deque.name: pushBack
Deque.documentation:
Inserts one value after the current last element. Exactly one value of the declared element type is required. Returns void and increases size by one. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.popBack()!);}
```

Expected output: 2.

Ownership: Owned values transfer into the queue; scalar values copy. Borrowed payloads retain their original owners. The receiver must allow mutation.

Deque.name: popFront
Deque.documentation:
Removes and returns the first element, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. A successful removal decreases size by one. An empty queue stays empty. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.popFront()!,values.size);}
```

Expected output: 4 1.

Ownership: The removed value transfers to the caller without cloning. Borrowed payloads retain their original owners. The receiver must allow mutation.

Deque.name: popBack
Deque.documentation:
Removes and returns the last element, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. A successful removal decreases size by one. An empty queue stays empty. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.popBack()!,values.size);}
```

Expected output: 2 1.

Ownership: The removed value transfers to the caller without cloning. Borrowed payloads retain their original owners. The receiver must allow mutation.

Deque.name: front
Deque.documentation:
Reads the first element, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. Returns Element | undefined and leaves the receiver unchanged. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.front()!,values.size);}
```

Expected output: 4 2.

Ownership: Scalar elements copy. Owned elements borrow readonly from a stored receiver and block its mutation or transfer while the borrow remains in scope. Temporary receivers cannot supply owned borrowed elements.

Deque.name: back
Deque.documentation:
Reads the last element, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. Returns Element | undefined and leaves the receiver unchanged. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.back()!,values.size);}
```

Expected output: 2 2.

Ownership: Scalar elements copy. Owned elements borrow readonly from a stored receiver and block its mutation or transfer while the borrow remains in scope. Temporary receivers cannot supply owned borrowed elements.

Deque.name: at
Deque.documentation:
Reads the element at a zero-based index counted from the front. Exactly one signed 64-bit int index is required. Negative indices and indices at or beyond size return undefined; negative indices do not count from the end. Returns Element | undefined and leaves the receiver unchanged. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.pushBack(2);console.log(values.at(1)!,values.at(-1)===undefined);}
```

Expected output: 2 true.

Ownership: Scalar elements copy. Owned elements borrow readonly from a stored receiver and block its mutation or transfer while the borrow remains in scope. Temporary receivers cannot supply owned borrowed elements.

Deque.name: clear
Deque.documentation:
Removes every element and sets size to zero. Takes no arguments and returns void. Clearing an empty queue has no effect. Wrong argument counts or incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(4);values.clear();console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 0.

Ownership: Stored owned values are released. The receiver must allow mutation. Existing view-owner restrictions remain conservatively active until the queue binding leaves scope.

std:collections.name: OrderedMap
std:collections.documentation:
An owned map that visits entries in ascending key order. new OrderedMap<K, V>() creates empty independent storage, takes no arguments and requires explicit key and value types. Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors. for...of borrows [key, value] entries without removing them. Spread into readonly tuple parameters borrows entries and leaves the map usable. Array spread and owning rest arguments transfer entries in ascending key order, consuming the map without cloning payloads. Array.from(map, mapper) supplies borrowed entries and zero-based indices in ascending key order; the mapper cannot mutate the map. Array.from(map) creates an independent entry snapshot when keys and values support cloning. clone(map) creates independent storage when both types support cloning; views remain non-cloneable.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);for(const entry of values){console.log(entry[0],entry[1]);}}
```

Expected output: a 1
b 2.

Ownership: set transfers owned keys and values. Borrowed views and callbacks retain their owner lifetimes. Traversal prevents receiver mutation or transfer. Storage releases when its owner ends.

examples.source: import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);for(const entry of values){console.log(entry[0],entry[1]);}}

std:collections.name: OrderedSet
std:collections.documentation:
An owned set that visits unique values in ascending key order. new OrderedSet<T>() takes no arguments and requires an explicit int, number, boolean, string or enum element type. Numbers compare numerically; signed zeros share one positive-zero key and all NaNs share one key greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. for...of visits each stored value once in ascending order without removing it. Empty sets perform no iterations. clone(set) creates independent storage. Call and array spread follow ascending order; scalar elements copy, readonly call arguments borrow strings, and owning string arguments transfer the set. Mutable key arguments are rejected. Ownership: add transfers owned keys; iteration borrows strings and prevents receiver mutation or transfer. Storage releases when its owner ends.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(3);values.add(1);values.add(3);for(const value of values){console.log(value);}console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 1
3
2.

examples.source: import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(3);values.add(1);values.add(3);for(const value of values){console.log(value);}console.log(values.size);}

std:collections.name: Deque
std:collections.documentation:
An owned double-ended queue of values of type T. Construct an empty queue with new Deque<T>(); the constructor takes no arguments and requires an explicit element type. Construction returns independent empty storage. Storage releases automatically when its owner ends. Record literals, comparison and inspection are currently unsupported. clone(queue) creates independent storage and deep-clones each element. It borrows the source without changing it. Cloning is rejected when any element contains a byte view, resource or callback that cannot be cloned. for...of visits elements from front to back without removing them. Scalar elements copy; owned elements borrow readonly for the iteration. Mutation or transfer of the queue during iteration is rejected. Empty queues perform no loop iterations. Call spread copies scalar elements, borrows owned elements for readonly parameters, or transfers the collection for owning parameters. Array spread copies scalars and transfers owned elements. Deque spread preserves front-to-back order; Heap spread order is unspecified. Mutable Heap element arguments are rejected to preserve heap ordering. Ownership: passing by value transfers the queue; borrowed element types retain their original owners.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections"; function accept(values:Deque<int>):void{} function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();accept(values);}
```

Expected output: none.

Records with readonly callbacks retain captured owners while stored or removed. A removed callback still borrows its captures.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";type Reader={read:ReadOnly<Function<int>>;};function main(){const text="hello";const values=new Deque<Reader>();values.pushBack({read:()=>text.length});for(const item of values){console.log(item.read());}}
```

Expected output: 5.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function sum(...values:int[]):int{let total=0;for(const value of values){total+=value;}return total;}function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(2);values.pushBack(3);console.log(sum(...values),values.size);}
```

Expected output: 5 2.

Nested readonly indexing borrows the stored array. It copies scalar elements and borrows owned elements; assignment through this view is rejected.

```tsrust
import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int[]>();values.pushBack([4,5]);console.log(values.front()![0],values.back()![1],values.size);}
```

Expected output: 4 5 1.

examples.source: import {Deque} from "std:collections"; function accept(values:Deque<int>):void{} function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();accept(values);}

import {Deque} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(2);values.pushFront(1);let sum=0;for(const value of values){sum+=value;}console.log(sum,values.size);}

import {Deque} from "std:collections";type Reader={read:ReadOnly<Function<int>>;};function main(){const text="hello";const values=new Deque<Reader>();values.pushBack({read:()=>text.length});for(const item of values){console.log(item.read());}}

import {Deque} from "std:collections";function sum(...values:int[]):int{let total=0;for(const value of values){total+=value;}return total;}function main(){const values=new Deque<int>();values.pushBack(2);values.pushBack(3);console.log(sum(...values),values.size);}

std:collections.name: Heap
std:collections.documentation:
An owned max heap: peek reads the greatest value and pop removes it. new Heap<T>() takes no arguments and requires an explicit int, number, boolean, string or enum element type. Numbers use numeric order, with all NaNs equal and greater than infinity; signed zeros are stored as positive zero. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order, without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place true above false. Enums use their backing values. Duplicate values remain separate entries. for...of borrows every stored element without removal in unspecified order. Scalar loop values copy; strings borrow readonly. Mutation or transfer during traversal is rejected. Repeated pop consumes values in descending order. clone(heap) deep-clones independent storage.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(2);values.push(9);console.log(values.pop()!,values.pop()!);}
```

Expected output: 9 2.

Call spread copies scalar elements, borrows owned elements for readonly parameters, or transfers the collection for owning parameters. Array spread copies scalars and transfers owned elements. Deque spread preserves front-to-back order; Heap spread order is unspecified. Mutable Heap element arguments are rejected to preserve heap ordering. Ownership: passing by value transfers the heap; storage releases automatically when its owner ends.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function sum(...values:int[]):int{let total=0;for(const value of values){total+=value;}return total;}function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(2);values.push(3);console.log(sum(...values),values.size);}
```

Expected output: 5 2.

examples.source: import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(2);values.push(9);let sum=0;for(const value of values){sum+=value;}console.log(sum,values.size);}

import {Heap} from "std:collections";function sum(...values:int[]):int{let total=0;for(const value of values){total+=value;}return total;}function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(2);values.push(3);console.log(sum(...values),values.size);}

std:fs.name: File
std:fs.documentation:
An owned open file with private storage. Use open for an existing read-only file, create for a new or truncated write-only file, read/write/writeAll for cursor operations, and close for explicit release. File literals, clone, comparison, hashing, console inspection and implicit sharing are unsupported. Unclosed files release automatically on scope exit. Explicit close consumes the handle even on failure; later use is rejected. No implicit flush or durability synchronization occurs. Ownership: passing by value transfers the handle; Mutable<File> borrows it for cursor-changing reads and writes.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {File} from "std:fs"; function inspect(file:ReadOnly<File>):void{} function main(){}
```

Expected output: none.

examples.source: import {File} from "std:fs"; function inspect(file:ReadOnly<File>):void{} function main(){}

std:fs.name: FsError
std:fs.signature: type FsError = { code: string; operation: string; message: string; osCode?: int; }
std:fs.documentation:
A file operation failure. code is a stable category: not-found, permission-denied, invalid-input, interrupted, is-directory, would-block, io, length-range, allocation, capacity-range or write-zero. operation names open, create, read, write, writeAll, readFile, writeFile, bufferReader, bufferWriter, flush or close. message explains the failure; its text is not stable. osCode preserves the platform error number when available, otherwise undefined. This record type takes no arguments and changes no file. Ownership: strings are owned; borrowing fields leaves the error reusable.

```tsrust
import {FsError} from "std:fs"; function main(){const error:FsError={code:"length-range",operation:"read",message:"Invalid length"};console.log(error.code,error.operation,error.osCode);}
```

Expected output: length-range read undefined.

code.documentation:
Stable failure category, as a string. Reading this field changes no file.

```tsrust
import {FsError} from "std:fs"; function main(){const error:FsError={code:"length-range",operation:"read",message:"Invalid length"};console.log(error.code,error.operation,error.osCode);}
```

Expected output: length-range read undefined. Ownership: string fields may be borrowed or explicitly cloned; osCode copies.

operation.documentation:
Operation that failed: open, create, read, write, writeAll, readFile, writeFile, bufferReader, bufferWriter, flush or close. Reading this field changes no file.

```tsrust
import {FsError} from "std:fs"; function main(){const error:FsError={code:"length-range",operation:"read",message:"Invalid length"};console.log(error.code,error.operation,error.osCode);}
```

Expected output: length-range read undefined. Ownership: string fields may be borrowed or explicitly cloned; osCode copies.

message.documentation:
Human-readable description. Text may vary by platform. Reading this field changes no file.

```tsrust
import {FsError} from "std:fs"; function main(){const error:FsError={code:"length-range",operation:"read",message:"Invalid length"};console.log(error.code,error.operation,error.osCode);}
```

Expected output: length-range read undefined. Ownership: string fields may be borrowed or explicitly cloned; osCode copies.

osCode.documentation:
Optional platform error number. Missing values read as undefined; range/allocation failures have no OS code. Reading this field changes no file.

```tsrust
import {FsError} from "std:fs"; function main(){const error:FsError={code:"length-range",operation:"read",message:"Invalid length"};console.log(error.code,error.operation,error.osCode);}
```

Expected output: length-range read undefined. Ownership: string fields may be borrowed or explicitly cloned; osCode copies.

std:fs.name: open

parameters.label: path: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Required path to an existing file. Relative paths use the process working directory; no default. Borrowed without mutation.

std:fs.documentation:
Opens an existing path read-only at cursor zero. Does not create or truncate files. Returns Ok(File) or an open error; missing paths, permissions and embedded NUL are reported. Opening a directory may succeed, but reading it fails. Paths follow normal filesystem symlink resolution. The example assumes input.bin exists. Ownership: path is borrowed; success creates a unique file owner.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {open,close} from "std:fs"; function main(){match(open("input.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(close(file)){Ok(_)=>{console.log("closed");},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: closed.

std:fs.name: read
std:fs.signature: read(file: Mutable<File | BufferedReader>, length: int): Result<Bytes, FsError>

parameters.label: file: Mutable<File | BufferedReader>
parameters.documentation: BufferedReader may read ahead by its capacity. Each call returns at most the currently buffered bytes, or one refill; short reads succeed. Required open file. Exclusively borrowed; a successful read advances its cursor by the returned byte count.

parameters.label: length: int
parameters.documentation: Required maximum byte count, 0 through 67108864 inclusive. No default. Zero returns empty Bytes without I/O.

std:fs.documentation:
BufferedReader may read ahead by its capacity. Each call returns at most the currently buffered bytes, or one refill; short reads succeed. Reads at most length bytes from the current cursor into independently owned Bytes. length is required and accepts 0 through 67108864 (64 MiB); zero returns empty bytes without I/O. There is no default length. Short reads and empty EOF results succeed; this does not read to the end automatically. Invalid lengths and allocation failures occur before I/O. Interrupted reads retry; other I/O errors return Err and retain the file for closing. No text decoding occurs. The example assumes input.bin contains four bytes. Ownership: mutably borrows the file, returns independent bytes and never closes the handle.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {open,read,close} from "std:fs"; import {length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(open("input.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(read(file,4)){Ok(bytes)=>{console.log(length(bytes));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}match(close(file)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: 4.

examples.source: import {open,read,close} from "std:fs"; import {length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(open("input.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(read(file,4)){Ok(bytes)=>{console.log(length(bytes));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}match(close(file)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}

std:fs.name: close
std:fs.signature: close(file: File | BufferedReader | BufferedWriter): Result<void, FsError>

parameters.label: file: File | BufferedReader | BufferedWriter
parameters.documentation: For BufferedWriter, close first attempts to flush pending bytes, then releases the descriptor even on failure. The first error wins; remaining bytes are discarded without retry. BufferedReader discards unread buffered bytes. Required owned open file. Consumed on both Ok and Err; later use and a second close are source errors.

std:fs.documentation:
For BufferedWriter, close first attempts to flush pending bytes, then releases the descriptor even on failure. The first error wins; remaining bytes are discarded without retry. BufferedReader discards unread buffered bytes. Releases a file and reports success as Ok(void), or an OS close failure as Err(FsError). The handle is consumed even when close fails. Close is not retried after an error. An unbuffered File has no user-space flush. No handle performs durability synchronization. Unclosed owners have a nonthrowing scope-exit fallback that discards close errors. The example assumes input.bin exists. Ownership: consumes the handle; no closed handle is returned.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {open,close} from "std:fs"; function main(){match(open("input.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(close(file)){Ok(_)=>{console.log("closed");},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: closed.

std:fs.name: create

parameters.label: path: string
parameters.documentation: Required filesystem path. Relative paths use the process working directory. Existing files are truncated; parent directories must exist.

std:fs.documentation:
Creates a write-only file, or truncates an existing file to zero bytes. Returns Ok(File) positioned at the beginning, or Err(FsError) for filesystem failures such as a missing parent or denied access. Existing permissions are preserved; new files use host permissions and umask. This does not create parent directories. There are no optional arguments.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {create} from "std:fs"; function main(){match(create("output.bin")){Ok(file)=>{console.log("created");},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: created.

Ownership: Returns one owned file. Explicit close consumes it and reports close errors; scope exit closes it automatically.

std:fs.name: write
std:fs.signature: write(file: Mutable<File | BufferedWriter>, bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>): Result<int, FsError>

parameters.label: file: Mutable<File | BufferedWriter>
parameters.documentation: BufferedWriter may accept bytes into memory before any file write. The returned count includes those bytes; flush or close sends pending bytes. An input at least as large as capacity bypasses the buffer after flushing pending bytes. Required writable file. Its cursor advances by the number of bytes successfully written.

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Required borrowed byte storage, from 0 through 67108864 bytes. Views write only their selected range. Storage is not mutated or copied.

std:fs.documentation:
BufferedWriter may accept bytes into memory before any file write. The returned count includes those bytes; flush or close sends pending bytes. An input at least as large as capacity bypasses the buffer after flushing pending bytes. Writes once at the current cursor and returns Ok(count), where count may be smaller than the input length, including zero. Retry the unwritten suffix when needed. Accepts 0 through 67108864 bytes; larger inputs return length-range before I/O. Empty input succeeds without I/O. Interrupted writes retry; other failures return Err(FsError) and leave the file available. Errors may follow partial writes; changes are not rolled back. The file cursor advances, but input bytes are unchanged. No durability synchronization occurs. Arguments are required; byte lengths do not count Unicode characters.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {create,write} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(create("output.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(fromUtf8("ABC")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(write(file,bytes)){Ok(count)=>{console.log(count);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: 3.

Ownership: Mutably borrows the file and reads the byte owner or view for this call. Neither argument is consumed; no byte loan escapes.

examples.source: import {create,write} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(create("output.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(fromUtf8("ABC")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(write(file,bytes)){Ok(count)=>{console.log(count);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}

std:fs.name: writeAll
std:fs.signature: writeAll(file: Mutable<File | BufferedWriter>, bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>): Result<void, FsError>

parameters.label: file: Mutable<File | BufferedWriter>
parameters.documentation: BufferedWriter may retain accepted bytes in memory. Success means the whole input was accepted; flush or close sends pending bytes. Required writable file. Its cursor advances by the number of bytes successfully written.

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Required borrowed byte storage, from 0 through 67108864 bytes. Views write only their selected range. Storage is not mutated or copied.

std:fs.documentation:
BufferedWriter may retain accepted bytes in memory. Success means the whole input was accepted; flush or close sends pending bytes. Writes the entire byte range at the current cursor, retrying short writes, and returns Ok(void). A zero-progress write returns Err with code write-zero. Accepts 0 through 67108864 bytes; larger inputs return length-range before I/O. Empty input succeeds without I/O. Interrupted writes retry; other failures return Err(FsError) and leave the file available. Errors may follow partial writes; changes are not rolled back. The file cursor advances, but input bytes are unchanged. No durability synchronization occurs. Arguments are required; byte lengths do not count Unicode characters.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {create,writeAll} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(create("output.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(fromUtf8("ABC")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(writeAll(file,bytes)){Ok(_)=>{console.log("written");},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: written.

Ownership: Mutably borrows the file and reads the byte owner or view for this call. Neither argument is consumed; no byte loan escapes.

examples.source: import {create,writeAll} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(create("output.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(fromUtf8("ABC")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(writeAll(file,bytes)){Ok(_)=>{console.log("written");},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}

std:fs.name: readFile
std:fs.signature: readFile(path: string, maxBytes?: int): Result<Bytes, FsError>

parameters.label: path: string
parameters.documentation: Required existing file path, resolved from the process working directory when relative.

parameters.label: maxBytes?: int
parameters.documentation: Maximum result size, 0 through 67108864 bytes. Defaults to 67108864. Invalid limits fail before opening the path.

std:fs.documentation:
Reads a file through EOF into independent owned bytes, then closes it. Returns Ok(Bytes), or Err(FsError). maxBytes defaults to 67108864 (64 MiB) and accepts 0 through 67108864. An empty file succeeds with a zero limit. An oversized file returns length-range; the reader consumes at most one extra byte to detect excess. This bound is enforced during reading, including when a file grows. Interrupted and short reads are handled. Allocation, read, open and close errors are reported. An earlier I/O failure takes precedence over a close error. No text decoding occurs. The example assumes input.bin contains four bytes.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {readFile} from "std:fs";import {length} from "std:bytes";function main(){match(readFile("input.bin",4)){Ok(bytes)=>{console.log(length(bytes));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: 4.

Ownership: Borrows the path and returns an owned buffer. No file handle escapes; the internal handle is closed on success and failure.

std:fs.name: writeFile
std:fs.signature: writeFile(path: string, bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>): Result<void, FsError>

parameters.label: path: string
parameters.documentation: Required output path. Creates a file or truncates an existing file. Parent directories must exist.

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Required borrowed byte range, 0 through 67108864 bytes. Length validation happens before creating or truncating the destination.

std:fs.documentation:
Creates or truncates a file, writes all input bytes, and closes it. Returns Ok(void), or Err(FsError). Accepts owned bytes, readonly views and mutable views; only a view’s selected range is written. Input must contain at most 67108864 bytes (64 MiB); oversized input returns length-range before the destination changes. Empty input creates or truncates an empty file. Short and interrupted writes retry; zero progress returns write-zero. Other I/O failures may leave a partial file. This operation is not an atomic replacement and performs no durability synchronization. Close errors are reported unless an earlier operation already failed. Input bytes are unchanged; no arguments are optional.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {writeFile} from "std:fs";import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes";function main(){match(fromUtf8("ABC")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(writeFile("output.bin",bytes)){Ok(_)=>{console.log("written");},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: written.

Ownership: Borrows the path and byte storage for this call. No borrowed data or file handle escapes; the internal file is closed on success and failure.

std:fs.name: BufferedReader
std:fs.documentation:
BufferedReader uniquely owns a File and its byte buffer. Reads return independent Bytes and may read ahead by the buffer capacity. Close discards unread bytes. No durability synchronization occurs. The type has no public fields or literal constructor and does not support cloning, inspection or sharing. Ownership: use Mutable<BufferedReader> for cursor operations; passing by value transfers ownership.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {open,bufferReader,close} from "std:fs"; function main(){match(open("input.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(bufferReader(file,4)){Ok(buffer)=>{match(close(buffer)){Ok(_)=>{console.log("closed");},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}
```

Expected output: closed.

std:fs.name: BufferedWriter
std:fs.documentation:
BufferedWriter uniquely owns a File and its byte buffer. Writes may retain bytes in memory until flush or close. Explicit close flushes once and releases the file even on error; scope cleanup does the same but discards errors. Use explicit close when errors matter. No durability synchronization occurs. The type has no public fields or literal constructor and does not support cloning, inspection or sharing. Ownership: use Mutable<BufferedWriter> for cursor operations; passing by value transfers ownership.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {open,bufferWriter,close} from "std:fs"; function main(){match(open("input.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(bufferWriter(file,4)){Ok(buffer)=>{match(close(buffer)){Ok(_)=>{console.log("closed");},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}
```

Expected output: closed.

std:fs.name: flush

parameters.label: writer: Mutable<BufferedWriter>
parameters.documentation: Required buffered writer. Exclusively borrowed, retained after success or failure.

std:fs.documentation:
Sends pending buffered bytes to the file and returns Ok(void), or Err(FsError). Retries interrupted and short writes; zero progress reports write-zero. On failure, bytes already written are removed and the unwritten suffix remains for an explicit retry. Empty buffers succeed without a data write. Does not synchronize durable storage. Ownership: mutably borrows the writer without consuming it.

File operations currently support macOS and Linux; other targets produce a native compilation diagnostic.

```tsrust
import {create,bufferWriter,flush,close} from "std:fs"; function main(){match(create("flush.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(bufferWriter(file)){Ok(writer)=>{match(flush(writer)){Ok(_)=>{console.log("flushed");},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}} match(close(writer)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}
```

Expected output: flushed.

std:bytes.name: fromArray

parameters.label: values: ReadOnly<int[]>
parameters.documentation: Integers to copy, each in 0..255. Borrowed without mutation; an empty array succeeds.

std:bytes.documentation:
Copies an integer array into a new owned byte buffer. Each element must be in 0..255. Returns Ok(buffer) on success, including an empty buffer for an empty array. Returns Err with code byte-range and the first invalid element offset when validation fails; length-range for a byte count outside int range, or allocation when reservation fails. No partial buffer escapes. The input array is unchanged. Reservation errors are recoverable; process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable.

```tsrust
import { fromArray, length } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromArray([0, 65, 255])) { Ok(bytes) => { console.log(length(bytes)); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }
```

Expected output: 3.

Ownership: borrows the array and returns an independent byte owner; no input elements are transferred.

std:bytes.name: length

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Byte buffer to observe. Borrowed without copying or mutation. Also accepts a ByteView or ByteViewMut; indices and counts are relative to the view.

std:bytes.documentation:
Returns the number of bytes in a buffer as int. Takes one byte buffer and does not change it. An empty buffer has length 0. The count measures bytes, never Unicode characters; for example, UTF-8 text may use several bytes per character. There are no operation errors for a valid buffer.

```tsrust
import { fromArray, length } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromArray([])) { Ok(bytes) => { console.log(length(bytes)); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }
```

Expected output: 0.

Ownership: borrows the buffer; the count copies and the buffer remains reusable.

std:bytes.name: at
std:bytes.signature: at(bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>, index: int): Result<int, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Byte buffer to read. Borrowed without copying or mutation. Also accepts a ByteView or ByteViewMut; indices and counts are relative to the view.

parameters.label: index: int
parameters.documentation: Zero-based byte index, from 0 through length(bytes) - 1. Negative indices never wrap.

std:bytes.documentation:
Reads one byte as an int in 0..255. Takes a byte buffer and a zero-based int index; the index must be nonnegative and smaller than the buffer length. Negative indices do not wrap. Returns Ok(value) without changing the buffer, or Err with code index-range, message "Byte index must be within the buffer.", and offset equal to the requested index. Every index fails on an empty buffer. Indices count bytes, not Unicode characters.

```tsrust
import { fromArray, at } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromArray([65, 255])) { Ok(bytes) => { match (at(bytes, 1)) { Ok(value) => { console.log(value); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }
```

Expected output: 255.

Ownership: borrows the buffer; the returned scalar copies and the buffer remains reusable.

std:bytes.name: set
std:bytes.signature: set(bytes: Mutable<Bytes | ByteViewMut>, index: int, value: int): Result<void, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: Mutable<Bytes | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Byte buffer to change through an exclusive borrow. The buffer length stays unchanged. Also accepts a ByteViewMut; indices are relative to the view and the write changes the owner.

parameters.label: index: int
parameters.documentation: Zero-based byte index, from 0 through length(bytes) - 1. Bounds are checked before the value.

parameters.label: value: int
parameters.documentation: Replacement byte in 0..255. Invalid values return byte-range without modifying the buffer.

std:bytes.documentation:
Replaces one byte without changing the buffer length. Takes an exclusively borrowed byte buffer, a nonnegative int index smaller than its length, and an int value in 0..255. Returns Ok() on success. Bounds are checked first: an invalid index returns Err with code index-range and the requested index as offset. With a valid index, an invalid value returns byte-range and that index as offset. Either failure leaves all bytes unchanged. Empty buffers reject every index; negative indices never wrap. Indices count bytes, not Unicode characters.

```tsrust
import { fromArray, at, set } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromArray([65])) { Ok(bytes) => { match (set(bytes, 0, 90)) { Ok(_) => { match (at(bytes, 0)) { Ok(value) => { console.log(value); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }
```

Expected output: 90.

Ownership: borrows the buffer exclusively for the call; it neither consumes nor clones the owner. Read access can resume after the call.

std:bytes.name: alloc
std:bytes.signature: alloc(length: int, fill?: int): Result<Bytes, ByteError>

parameters.label: length: int
parameters.documentation: Nonnegative byte count that fits native storage.

parameters.label: fill?: int
parameters.documentation: Initial byte in 0..255; defaults to 0, including omitted arguments.

std:bytes.documentation:
Creates an independent owned byte buffer of the requested length. Every byte is initialized to fill, which defaults to 0. Returns Ok(buffer), including an empty buffer for length 0. Length must be nonnegative and fit native storage; fill must be an int in 0..255. Length is validated before fill, and fill is validated even for an empty buffer. Invalid arguments return Err with code length-range or byte-range and an undefined offset. Failed storage reservation returns allocation with an undefined offset; no partial buffer escapes. Process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable. Length counts bytes, not Unicode characters.

```tsrust
import {alloc,length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(alloc(3)){Ok(bytes)=>{console.log(length(bytes));},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}}
```

Expected output: 3.

Ownership: returns an independent byte owner; no existing buffer is borrowed or consumed.

std:bytes.name: resize
std:bytes.signature: resize(bytes: Mutable<Bytes>, length: int, fill?: int): Result<void, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: Mutable<Bytes>
parameters.documentation: Buffer to resize through an exclusive borrow.

parameters.label: length: int
parameters.documentation: New nonnegative byte count that fits native storage.

parameters.label: fill?: int
parameters.documentation: Byte in 0..255 used only for newly added bytes; defaults to 0. Validated even when shrinking.

std:bytes.documentation:
Changes a buffer to the requested byte length while preserving its existing prefix. Growth initializes new bytes to fill, which defaults to 0. Shrinking removes trailing bytes and may retain storage capacity; discarded bytes do not reappear after growth. Returns Ok() on success. Length must be nonnegative and fit native storage; fill must be an int in 0..255. Length is validated before fill, even when the length stays unchanged or becomes 0. Invalid arguments return Err with code length-range or byte-range and an undefined offset. Failed growth reservation returns allocation with an undefined offset. Every failure leaves length and contents unchanged. Process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable. Length counts bytes, not Unicode characters.

```tsrust
import {alloc,resize,length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(alloc(1)){Ok(bytes)=>{match(resize(bytes,3,65)){Ok(_)=>{console.log(length(bytes));},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}}
```

Expected output: 3.

Ownership: borrows the buffer exclusively for the call; it neither consumes nor clones the owner.

std:bytes.name: append
std:bytes.signature: append(bytes: Mutable<Bytes>, values: ReadOnly<int[]>): Result<void, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: Mutable<Bytes>
parameters.documentation: Buffer to extend through an exclusive borrow.

parameters.label: values: ReadOnly<int[]>
parameters.documentation: Integers in 0..255 to append in order. The array is borrowed and unchanged.

std:bytes.documentation:
Adds checked integer values to the end of a byte buffer in array order. Returns Ok() on success; an empty array succeeds without changing the buffer. Each value must be in 0..255. Checks the combined byte length first, then every input value, before reserving storage or changing contents. An invalid value returns byte-range with its index in the input array as offset. A combined length outside native storage returns length-range with an undefined offset. Failed reservation returns allocation with an undefined offset. Every failure preserves the original length and contents. Process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable. Byte values are copied explicitly from the array; no integer wrapping occurs.

```tsrust
import {fromArray,append,length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(fromArray([65])){Ok(bytes)=>{match(append(bytes,[0,255])){Ok(_)=>{console.log(length(bytes));},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}}
```

Expected output: 3.

Ownership: borrows the buffer exclusively and the array readonly for the call. Neither input is consumed or implicitly cloned.

std:bytes.name: copy
std:bytes.signature: copy(bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>, start: int, end: int): Result<Bytes, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Source buffer, borrowed without mutation. Also accepts a ByteView or ByteViewMut; indices and counts are relative to the view.

parameters.label: start: int
parameters.documentation: Inclusive starting byte index, from 0 through length(bytes). Checked before end.

parameters.label: end: int
parameters.documentation: Exclusive ending byte index, from start through length(bytes).

std:bytes.documentation:
Creates an independent owned buffer containing bytes in the half-open range [start, end). Returns Ok(buffer); start equal to end produces an empty buffer, including at the source end. Bounds must satisfy 0 <= start <= end <= length(bytes). Negative indices never wrap and bounds are not clamped. Checks start first, then end; an invalid range returns range with the first offending coordinate as offset. A reversed range reports end. Failed reservation returns allocation with an undefined offset. The source remains unchanged on success and failure. Changing either buffer afterward cannot change the other. Coordinates count bytes, not Unicode characters. Process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable.

```tsrust
import {fromArray,copy,length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(fromArray([0,65,255])){Ok(bytes)=>{match(copy(bytes,1,3)){Ok(part)=>{console.log(length(part));},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}}
```

Expected output: 2.

Ownership: borrows the source readonly and returns a new independent owner. Copying is explicit and does not transfer the source.

std:bytes.name: fromUtf8

parameters.label: text: string
parameters.documentation: Valid UTF-8 text to encode. Borrowed unchanged; no implicit conversion from other types.

std:bytes.documentation:
Copies the UTF-8 encoding of a string into an independent owned byte buffer. Takes exactly one string and returns Ok(buffer), including an empty buffer for empty text. Text is already valid UTF-8; no normalization, BOM stripping or replacement occurs. NUL bytes and multibyte Unicode scalars are preserved. Length counts encoded bytes rather than characters. A length outside native storage returns length-range; failed reservation returns allocation. Both errors omit offset. No partial buffer escapes. Process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable.

```tsrust
import {fromUtf8,length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(fromUtf8("é😀")){Ok(bytes)=>{console.log(length(bytes));},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}}
```

Expected output: 6.

Ownership: borrows the input and returns independent owned storage; no input is consumed or implicitly cloned.

std:bytes.name: toUtf8
std:bytes.signature: toUtf8(bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>): Result<string, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Byte buffer to decode strictly. Borrowed unchanged; invalid bytes are never replaced. Also accepts a ByteView or ByteViewMut; indices and counts are relative to the view.

std:bytes.documentation:
Decodes a byte buffer strictly into an independent owned UTF-8 string. Takes exactly one byte buffer and returns Ok(text), including an empty string for an empty buffer. Invalid, overlong, surrogate or truncated sequences return utf8 with message "Byte buffer contains invalid UTF-8." and offset equal to the first invalid sequence start in bytes. No replacement characters are inserted. NUL and a leading U+FEFF are preserved; no normalization or BOM stripping occurs. Valid text is checked once, then copied to reserved output storage. Failed reservation returns allocation with an undefined offset. The buffer is unchanged on success and failure. Process-wide memory exhaustion is not guaranteed to be recoverable.

```tsrust
import {fromArray,toUtf8} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(fromArray([195,169,240,159,152,128])){Ok(bytes)=>{match(toUtf8(bytes)){Ok(text)=>{console.log(text);},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.message);}}}
```

Expected output: é😀.

Ownership: borrows the input and returns independent owned storage; no input is consumed or implicitly cloned.

std:bytes.name: ByteView
ByteViewMut
view
std:bytes.signature: view(bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>, start: int, end: int): Result<ByteView, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Byte owner or view to look into without copying or mutation. A readonly ByteView forwards its byte owner lifetime; Bytes and ByteViewMut stay borrowed for the result lifetime.

parameters.label: start: int
parameters.documentation: Inclusive starting byte index, from 0 through length(bytes). Checked before end.

parameters.label: end: int
parameters.documentation: Exclusive ending byte index, from start through length(bytes).

std:bytes.documentation:
Returns a readonly window onto the bytes in the half-open range [start, end) without copying them. Returns Ok(view); start equal to end produces an empty view, including at the end of the bytes. Bounds must satisfy 0 <= start <= end <= length(bytes). Negative indices never wrap and bounds are not clamped. Checks start first, then end; an invalid range returns the error code range with the first offending coordinate as offset. A reversed range reports end. There is no allocation, so there is no allocation error. The view reads the owner's bytes: it has the same contents as the owner for as long as it exists. Coordinates count bytes, not Unicode characters; a range that splits a character makes toUtf8 of the view fail. A view of a view uses coordinates relative to that view. A readonly ByteView forwards the original byte owner lifetime, so the new view can outlive the intermediate view or its container. A ByteViewMut source remains borrowed for the result lifetime.

```tsrust
import { fromUtf8, view, toUtf8 } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromUtf8("hello")) { Ok(bytes) => { match (view(bytes, 1, 4)) { Ok(part) => { match (toUtf8(part)) { Ok(text) => { console.log(text); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }
```

Expected output: ell.

Ownership: borrows the bytes readonly. While the view is in scope the owner can be read and cannot be written, resized, moved or replaced. The view cannot be returned from the function that owns the bytes. Use copy for bytes that must outlive their owner.

import { fromUtf8, view, toUtf8 } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromUtf8("hello")) { Ok(bytes) => { match (view(bytes, 1, 4)) { Ok(part) => { match (toUtf8(part)) { Ok(text) => { console.log(text); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }

std:bytes.name: viewMut
std:bytes.signature: viewMut(bytes: Mutable<Bytes | ByteViewMut>, start: int, end: int): Result<ByteViewMut, ByteError>

parameters.label: bytes: Mutable<Bytes | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Byte owner or exclusive view to write into. Borrowed exclusively, without copying, for as long as the result is in scope.

parameters.label: start: int
parameters.documentation: Inclusive starting byte index, from 0 through length(bytes). Checked before end.

parameters.label: end: int
parameters.documentation: Exclusive ending byte index, from start through length(bytes).

std:bytes.documentation:
Returns an exclusive, writable window onto the bytes in the half-open range [start, end) without copying them. Returns Ok(view); start equal to end produces an empty view. Bounds must satisfy 0 <= start <= end <= length(bytes). Negative indices never wrap and bounds are not clamped. Checks start first, then end; an invalid range returns the error code range with the first offending coordinate as offset. A reversed range reports end. There is no allocation. set through the view changes the owner's bytes at start plus the view index. The view has a fixed length and cannot resize the owner. A readonly ByteView cannot supply an exclusive view.

```tsrust
import { fromUtf8, viewMut, set, toUtf8 } from "std:bytes";
function main() { match (fromUtf8("hello")) { Ok(bytes) => { match (viewMut(bytes, 0, 1)) { Ok(part) => { match (set(part, 0, 72)) { Ok(_) => {}, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } match (toUtf8(bytes)) { Ok(text) => { console.log(text); }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }, Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); }, } }
```

Expected output: Hello.

Ownership: borrows the bytes exclusively. While the view is in scope the owner cannot be read, written, resized, moved or replaced. The owner is usable again, with the written bytes, after the view's scope ends.
