OrderedSet.name: size
OrderedSet.documentation:
The number of distinct stored keys, including at most one NaN and one zero key. This read-only property takes no arguments, returns a nonnegative int, and does not change the set. Ownership: reading size borrows the receiver.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(2);console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 1.

OrderedSet.name: add
OrderedSet.documentation:
Insert value if no equal key is present. value must have the declared element type. A duplicate leaves size unchanged; signed zeros and NaNs follow the set equality rule. Returns void and may change the set. Ownership: an owned argument transfers even when it duplicates an existing key.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(2);values.add(2);console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 1.

OrderedSet.name: has
OrderedSet.documentation:
Test whether an equal key is stored. value must have the declared element type; an empty set returns false. Returns boolean without changing the set. Lookup follows the key order. Ownership: the receiver and argument are borrowed; string queries remain reusable and are not copied.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(2);console.log(values.has(2),values.has(9));}
```

Expected output: true false.

OrderedSet.name: delete
OrderedSet.documentation:
Remove the equal key if present. value must have the declared element type. Returns true after removal, or false when no key matched, including on an empty set. Ownership: the receiver is exclusively borrowed; the query argument is borrowed and remains reusable.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(2);console.log(values.delete(2),values.delete(2),values.size);}
```

Expected output: true false 0.

OrderedSet.name: clear
OrderedSet.documentation:
Remove all keys. Takes no arguments, returns void and leaves size zero. Clearing an empty set succeeds. Ownership: exclusively borrows the receiver and releases its stored keys.

```tsrust
import {OrderedSet} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedSet<int>();values.add(2);values.clear();console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 0.

Heap.name: size
Heap.documentation:
Returns the readonly number of stored values. Takes no arguments and leaves the heap unchanged. Invalid argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(3);console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 1.

Ownership: push, pop and clear require mutable access; peek and size borrow readonly. No implicit element cloning.

Heap.name: push
Heap.documentation:
Transfers one value of the declared element type into the heap. Returns void and increases size by one. Equal values are stored separately. Invalid argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(3);values.push(9);console.log(values.pop()!);}
```

Expected output: 9.

Ownership: push, pop and clear require mutable access; peek and size borrow readonly. No implicit element cloning.

Heap.name: peek
Heap.documentation:
Returns the greatest value without removal, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. Scalar results copy; owned string results borrow from a stored receiver. Mutation is rejected while that borrow remains live. Invalid argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(3);console.log(values.peek(),values.size);}
```

Expected output: 3 1.

Ownership: push, pop and clear require mutable access; peek and size borrow readonly. No implicit element cloning.

Heap.name: pop
Heap.documentation:
Removes and returns the greatest value, or undefined when empty. Takes no arguments. Removal transfers an owned value to the caller. Invalid argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(3);console.log(values.pop(),values.size,values.pop());}
```

Expected output: 3 0 undefined.

Ownership: push, pop and clear require mutable access; peek and size borrow readonly. No implicit element cloning.

Heap.name: clear
Heap.documentation:
Releases every stored value and sets size to zero. Takes no arguments and returns void. Invalid argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {Heap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new Heap<int>();values.push(3);values.clear();console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 0.

Ownership: push, pop and clear require mutable access; peek and size borrow readonly. No implicit element cloning.

OrderedMap.name: size
OrderedMap.documentation:
Returns the number of distinct keys as int. Readonly property with no arguments; assignment is rejected. Empty maps have size 0. The receiver is unchanged.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 2

Ownership: Reading size borrows the receiver.

OrderedMap.name: set
OrderedMap.documentation:
Inserts key and value, or replaces the value of an equal key. Takes exactly two arguments matching Key and Value; returns void. Replacing a key leaves size unchanged. Traversal remains in ascending key order.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);values.set("a",3);console.log(values.size,values.get("a")!);}
```

Expected output: 2 3

Ownership: Owned arguments transfer into the map. Replacement releases the previous value; stored views retain their original owner loans.

OrderedMap.name: get
OrderedMap.documentation:
Reads the value for key, or returns undefined when absent. Takes one key argument. The receiver is unchanged for a stored map. No default value is inserted.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.get("a") ?? 0,values.get("missing") ?? 0);}
```

Expected output: 1 0

Ownership: The key is borrowed. Scalar results copy; owned results from a stored map borrow readonly. A consumed temporary transfers its selected owned value and releases the other entries.

OrderedMap.name: has
OrderedMap.documentation:
Returns true when key is present and false otherwise. Takes one key argument and leaves the receiver unchanged.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.has("a"),values.has("missing"));}
```

Expected output: true false

Ownership: Receiver and owned query key are borrowed.

OrderedMap.name: delete
OrderedMap.documentation:
Removes key and its value, returning true if present or false if absent. Takes one key argument. Successful removal reduces size by one; deleting an absent key changes nothing.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.delete("a"),values.delete("a"),values.size);}
```

Expected output: true false 1

Ownership: The query key is borrowed. Removal releases the stored key and value. Retained entry borrows prevent mutation.

OrderedMap.name: clear
OrderedMap.documentation:
Removes every entry and returns void. Takes no arguments. Size becomes 0; clearing an empty map is valid.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);values.clear();console.log(values.size);}
```

Expected output: 0

Ownership: Removed keys and values are released. Retained entry borrows prevent mutation.

OrderedMap.name: keys
OrderedMap.documentation:
Returns an independent array of keys in ascending key order. Takes no arguments, leaves the receiver unchanged and returns an empty array for an empty map.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.keys().join(","));}
```

Expected output: a,b

Ownership: Keys are explicitly copied or cloned into independent array storage.

OrderedMap.name: values
OrderedMap.documentation:
Returns an independent array of values in ascending key order. Takes no arguments and leaves the receiver unchanged. Empty maps produce an empty array. Values must support independent cloning; views and other non-cloneable values are rejected.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);console.log(values.values().join(","));}
```

Expected output: 1,2

Ownership: Values are explicitly deep-cloned into independent array storage.

OrderedMap.name: entries
OrderedMap.documentation:
Returns an independent array of [key, value] tuples in ascending key order. Takes no arguments and leaves the receiver unchanged. Empty maps produce an empty array. Both payload types must support independent cloning.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);const pairs=values.entries();console.log(pairs[0][0],pairs[0][1]);}
```

Expected output: a 1

Ownership: Keys and values are explicitly deep-cloned. Use for...of for borrowed entry traversal.

OrderedMap.name: forEach
OrderedMap.signature: forEach(callback: (value: Value, key: Key, source: OrderedMap<Key, Value>) => Result): void
parameters: callback: (value: Value, key: Key, source: OrderedMap<Key, Value>) => Result
OrderedMap.documentation:
Calls callback once for each entry in ascending key order, supplying value, key and source. Takes one callback; the callback may omit trailing parameters. Returns void and ignores callback return values. An empty map makes no calls. The receiver is unchanged; callback failures propagate.

Keys must match the declared int, number, boolean, string or enum type; mixed unions and object identity keys are unsupported. Numbers use numeric order, with signed zeros equal and NaNs equal and greater than infinity. Strings use Unicode scalar lexicographic order without locale collation or normalization. Booleans place false before true; enums use their backing values. Wrong argument counts and incompatible types are static errors.

```tsrust
import {OrderedMap} from "std:collections";function main(){const values=new OrderedMap<string,int>();values.set("b",2);values.set("a",1);let text="";values.forEach((value,key)=>{text+=key+String(value)+"|";});console.log(text);}
```

Expected output: a1|b2|

Ownership: Traversal borrows the receiver and owned payloads. Receiver mutation or transfer during traversal is rejected.

std:env.name: EnvError
std:env.signature: type EnvError = { code: string; message: string }
std:env.documentation:
Describes an environment lookup failure. code is InvalidName for an empty name or a name containing = or NUL, or NotUnicode when a value cannot be represented as Unicode. message explains the failure without including the environment value. Missing variables are successful lookups, not errors. Fields are ordinary strings.

```tsrust
import {EnvError} from "std:env"; function describe(error:ReadOnly<EnvError>):string{return error.code + ": " + error.message;} function main(){}
```

Expected output: none. Ownership: an owned record; explicit clone creates independent storage.

examples.source: import {EnvError} from "std:env"; function describe(error:ReadOnly<EnvError>):string{return error.code + ": " + error.message;} function main(){}

std:env.name: get

parameters.label: name: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Required nonempty variable name. Must not contain = or NUL. Uses the executable host’s case-sensitivity rules.

std:env.documentation:
Reads a variable from the running process environment. Returns Ok(value) with an independent UTF-8 string when present, Ok(undefined) when missing, or Err(EnvError). An empty value returns Ok(""). Empty names and names containing = or NUL fail with InvalidName. Non-Unicode values fail with NotUnicode; no lossy replacement occurs. Lookup uses host name matching rules and does not mutate the environment. Values are read at execution time.

```tsrust
import {get} from "std:env"; function main(){match(get("A=B")){Ok(_)=>{throw "unexpected success";},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);}}}
```

Expected output: InvalidName. Ownership: borrows name without consuming it; successful strings own their storage.

std:time.name: monotonicNow
std:time.documentation:
Measures elapsed time using a process-local monotonic clock. Takes no arguments and has no defaults or argument errors. Returns a nonnegative number of milliseconds, including fractional milliseconds, relative to an origin established by the first call. Subtract two readings from the same process to measure a duration; readings are not calendar timestamps and must not be compared across processes. Consecutive readings may be equal because clock resolution varies. System-clock adjustments do not change the origin. Whether suspended time counts is platform dependent, and floating-point precision decreases over long runtimes. No receiver is mutated.

```tsrust
import { monotonicNow } from "std:time";
function main() { const start = monotonicNow(); const elapsed = monotonicNow() - start; console.log(elapsed >= 0); } // prints true
```

Ownership: returns an independent number; no handle, borrowing or explicit cleanup is required.

examples.source:
import { monotonicNow } from "std:time";
function main() { const start = monotonicNow(); const elapsed = monotonicNow() - start; console.log(elapsed >= 0); }

std:json.name: borrowRaw
std:json.signature: borrowRaw(text: string, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>): Result<JsonRaw, JsonError>

parameters.label: text: string
parameters.documentation: Named source string containing one strict JSON value, with optional surrounding whitespace. Validation does not modify or copy the source.

parameters.label: limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>
parameters.documentation: Nonnegative input limits: maxBytes defaults to 16777216, maxDepth to 64, maxEntries and maxNodes to 1000000. Depth cannot exceed 64. Whitespace and duplicate fields count toward their budgets.

std:json.documentation:
Validates one strict JSON value and returns a source-backed JsonRaw fragment. Optional limits default to maxBytes 16777216, maxDepth 64, maxEntries 1000000 and maxNodes 1000000. All limits must be nonnegative; depth cannot exceed 64. Whitespace and duplicate fields count toward budgets. Rejects comments, trailing data, malformed escapes and invalid resource limits with JsonError codes and zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets. No dynamic value tree is built. Validation can allocate temporary escape scratch; the returned fragment retains no copied source buffer. JSON.stringify and JSON.tryStringify preserve raw source text exactly, including whitespace, key order, escapes and number spelling. Raw fragments count toward the enclosing 64-container depth limit and output byte limit. JSONL writing preserves single-line raw text; literal CR or LF returns record-newline before writing any bytes of that record. Escaped newline sequences remain valid.

```tsrust
import {borrowRaw} from 'std:json';function main(){const text='{ "count": 7e0 }';match(borrowRaw(text)){Ok(raw)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(raw));},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);}}}
```

Expected output: { "count": 7e0 }.

Ownership: the fragment borrows text. Its source must remain alive and cannot be replaced or moved while the fragment is used. The fragment cannot be cloned or constructed directly. Errors carry no source loan.

std:json.name: JsonRaw
std:json.documentation:
A validated fragment borrowing its original JSON source. Create it with borrowRaw or select it as a field type in JSON.parse<T>/JSON.tryParse<T>; direct construction and clone are rejected. It is distinct from an owned JsonValue or a child JsonView. JSON.stringify and JSON.tryStringify preserve raw source text exactly, including whitespace, key order, escapes and number spelling. Raw fragments count toward the enclosing 64-container depth limit and output byte limit. JSONL writing preserves single-line raw text; literal CR or LF returns record-newline before writing any bytes of that record. Escaped newline sequences remain valid.

```tsrust
import {borrowRaw} from 'std:json';function main(){const text='{ "count": 7e0 }';match(borrowRaw(text)){Ok(raw)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(raw));},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);}}}
```

Expected output: { "count": 7e0 }

Ownership: the original source must outlive every use of this fragment.

Typed decoding: Explicit JsonRaw fields preserve the selected value's source tokens without constructing a dynamic subtree. Their source text must outlive every use; containing values cannot be cloned. Raw fields work in strict JSON typed decoding, including arrays and optional fields; JSONC and JSONL typed decoding still require owned fields.

std:json.name: JsonBuildLimits
std:json.documentation:
Construction budgets with required int fields maxDepth, maxEntries and maxNodes. Omitted limits default to maxDepth 64, maxEntries 1000000 and maxNodes 1000000. All limits must be nonnegative integers; maxDepth cannot exceed 64. The root counts as one value and one container level. maxEntries applies to every nested collection; maxNodes counts the root and all descendant values. Zero entries permits an empty container; zero depth or nodes rejects any container. Errors use depth-limit, entry-limit, node-limit or invalid-limits with offset zero. Existing inputs are already allocated; these limits bound the resulting tree, not an input byte stream. No receiver is mutated. Ownership: ordinary owned record, borrowed by constructors.

```tsrust
import {fromArray,fromInt,JsonValue,JsonBuildLimits} from "std:json";function main(){const values:JsonValue[]=[fromInt(42)];const limits:JsonBuildLimits={maxDepth:1,maxEntries:1,maxNodes:2};match(fromArray(values,limits)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: [42].

std:json.name: JsonEntry
std:json.documentation:
An owned object-entry record with key:string and value:JsonValue fields. Used in fromEntries input arrays. Keys are literal UTF-8 text, including empty keys; no path interpretation occurs. The last duplicate key wins. Ownership: constructing an entry transfers owned fields; explicit clone copies supported contents independently.

```tsrust
import {fromEntries,fromInt,JsonEntry} from "std:json";function main(){const entries:JsonEntry[]=[{key:"answer",value:fromInt(42)}];match(fromEntries(entries)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: {"answer":42}.

std:json.name: fromArray
std:json.signature: fromArray(values: Owned<JsonValue[]>, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonBuildLimits>): Result<JsonValue, JsonError>

parameters.label: values: Owned<JsonValue[]>
parameters.documentation: Ordered child values. Consumed on success and failure; use clone(values) to retain the input.

parameters.label: limits?: ReadOnly<JsonBuildLimits>
parameters.documentation: Omitted limits default to maxDepth 64, maxEntries 1000000 and maxNodes 1000000. All limits must be nonnegative integers; maxDepth cannot exceed 64. The root counts as one value and one container level. maxEntries applies to every nested collection; maxNodes counts the root and all descendant values. Zero entries permits an empty container; zero depth or nodes rejects any container. Errors use depth-limit, entry-limit, node-limit or invalid-limits with offset zero. Existing inputs are already allocated; these limits bound the resulting tree, not an input byte stream.

std:json.documentation:
Constructs an owned JSON array in input order, moving child values without parsing or deep copies. Empty input produces []. Returns Ok(JsonValue) or Err(JsonError). Container storage may allocate. Omitted limits default to maxDepth 64, maxEntries 1000000 and maxNodes 1000000. All limits must be nonnegative integers; maxDepth cannot exceed 64. The root counts as one value and one container level. maxEntries applies to every nested collection; maxNodes counts the root and all descendant values. Zero entries permits an empty container; zero depth or nodes rejects any container. Errors use depth-limit, entry-limit, node-limit or invalid-limits with offset zero. Existing inputs are already allocated; these limits bound the resulting tree, not an input byte stream. Ownership: consumes the array and children on success or failure; limits is borrowed and unchanged.

```tsrust
import {fromArray,fromInt,JsonValue,JsonBuildLimits} from "std:json";function main(){const values:JsonValue[]=[fromInt(42)];const limits:JsonBuildLimits={maxDepth:1,maxEntries:1,maxNodes:2};match(fromArray(values,limits)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: [42].

std:json.name: fromEntries
std:json.signature: fromEntries(entries: Owned<JsonEntry[]>, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonBuildLimits>): Result<JsonValue, JsonError>

parameters.label: entries: Owned<JsonEntry[]>
parameters.documentation: Owned key/value entries, consumed on success and failure. Duplicate keys use the last supplied value.

parameters.label: limits?: ReadOnly<JsonBuildLimits>
parameters.documentation: Omitted limits default to maxDepth 64, maxEntries 1000000 and maxNodes 1000000. All limits must be nonnegative integers; maxDepth cannot exceed 64. The root counts as one value and one container level. maxEntries applies to every nested collection; maxNodes counts the root and all descendant values. Zero entries permits an empty container; zero depth or nodes rejects any container. Errors use depth-limit, entry-limit, node-limit or invalid-limits with offset zero. Existing inputs are already allocated; these limits bound the resulting tree, not an input byte stream.

std:json.documentation:
Constructs an owned JSON object from key/value records. Empty input produces {}. The last duplicate key wins, and output keys use the existing sorted-key representation. All supplied entries and their descendant values count against limits before duplicate replacement. Returns Ok(JsonValue) or Err(JsonError), without parsing or deep-copying child values. Object storage allocates. Omitted limits default to maxDepth 64, maxEntries 1000000 and maxNodes 1000000. All limits must be nonnegative integers; maxDepth cannot exceed 64. The root counts as one value and one container level. maxEntries applies to every nested collection; maxNodes counts the root and all descendant values. Zero entries permits an empty container; zero depth or nodes rejects any container. Errors use depth-limit, entry-limit, node-limit or invalid-limits with offset zero. Existing inputs are already allocated; these limits bound the resulting tree, not an input byte stream. Ownership: consumes entries, keys and values on success or failure; limits is borrowed and unchanged.

```tsrust
import {fromEntries,fromInt,JsonEntry} from "std:json";function main(){const entries:JsonEntry[]=[{key:"answer",value:fromInt(42)}];match(fromEntries(entries)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: {"answer":42}.

std:json.name: nullValue
std:json.documentation:
Creates an owned JSON null value. Takes no arguments and performs no parsing. Null is a present JSON value, distinct from a missing property or undefined. No receiver is mutated.

```tsrust
import {nullValue} from "std:json";function main(){console.log(JSON.stringify(nullValue()));}
```

Expected output: null.

Ownership: The result owns its value and supports explicit clone.

std:json.name: fromBoolean

parameters.label: value: boolean
parameters.documentation: Creates an owned JSON boolean from true or false without parsing or coercion. Copies the scalar argument; the caller may reuse it. No receiver is mutated.

std:json.documentation:
Creates an owned JSON boolean from true or false without parsing or coercion. Copies the scalar argument; the caller may reuse it. No receiver is mutated.

```tsrust
import {fromBoolean} from "std:json";function main(){console.log(JSON.stringify(fromBoolean(true)));}
```

Expected output: true.

Ownership: The result owns its value and supports explicit clone.

std:json.name: fromInt

parameters.label: value: int
parameters.documentation: Creates an owned JSON integer without parsing or floating-point conversion. Accepts the full signed 64-bit int range, including both endpoints, and preserves the exact value. Copies the argument. No receiver is mutated.

std:json.documentation:
Creates an owned JSON integer without parsing or floating-point conversion. Accepts the full signed 64-bit int range, including both endpoints, and preserves the exact value. Copies the argument. No receiver is mutated.

```tsrust
import {fromInt} from "std:json";function main(){console.log(JSON.stringify(fromInt(9223372036854775807)));}
```

Expected output: 9223372036854775807.

Ownership: The result owns its value and supports explicit clone.

std:json.name: fromNumber

parameters.label: value: number
parameters.documentation: Creates an owned JSON number from a finite floating-point value without parsing. Preserves negative zero and the supplied floating-point value. Returns Ok(JsonValue), or Err with code number-nonfinite and offset zero for NaN or either infinity. It cannot recover precision already lost before the call; use fromInt for exact integer construction. Copies the argument. No receiver is mutated.

std:json.documentation:
Creates an owned JSON number from a finite floating-point value without parsing. Preserves negative zero and the supplied floating-point value. Returns Ok(JsonValue), or Err with code number-nonfinite and offset zero for NaN or either infinity. It cannot recover precision already lost before the call; use fromInt for exact integer construction. Copies the argument. No receiver is mutated.

```tsrust
import {fromNumber} from "std:json";function main(){match(fromNumber(1.25)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: 1.25.

Ownership: The success value owns its storage and supports explicit clone.

std:json.name: fromString

parameters.label: value: Owned<string>
parameters.documentation: Creates a JSON string from UTF-8 text without parsing it as JSON. Empty text, Unicode, quotes and control characters remain string contents; stringify performs the required escaping. Transfers an owned string buffer without copying it; literal-backed strings allocate owned JSON text. No receiver is mutated.

std:json.documentation:
Creates a JSON string from UTF-8 text without parsing it as JSON. Empty text, Unicode, quotes and control characters remain string contents; stringify performs the required escaping. Transfers an owned string buffer without copying it; literal-backed strings allocate owned JSON text. No receiver is mutated.

```tsrust
import {fromString} from "std:json";function main(){console.log(JSON.stringify(fromString("hello")));}
```

Expected output: "hello".

Ownership: Consumes value. Use fromString(clone(text)) to preserve an existing string. Use String(view) first for a borrowed StringView.

std:json.name: StringView
std:json.documentation:
A read-only borrowed UTF-8 string returned by asString. Borrows the text of a JSON string without copying it. Accepts a JsonValue owner or JsonView; other JSON kinds return Err with code expected-string and offset zero. Returns Ok(StringView). The source is unchanged.

The view supports length, startsWith, endsWith, includes, indexOf and lastIndexOf. Length and search coordinates use UTF-8 bytes; explicit positions must be scalar boundaries. typeof returns string, Boolean(view) is false only for empty text, and console output displays the text. String(view) makes an independent owned string. Other string operations require that explicit conversion.

```tsrust
import {asString} from "std:json";function main(){const owner=JSON.parse('"hello"');match(asString(owner)){Ok(text)=>{console.log(typeof text,text.length,text.includes("ell"),String(text));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: string 5 true hello.

Ownership: the view may be stored or returned only while its source owner remains alive. The owner cannot be moved or replaced while the view is retained. clone(view) is rejected; use String(view) to copy. An error carries no source loan.

std:json.name: asString

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Named JSON owner or view containing string text. Non-string kinds return expected-string.

std:json.documentation:
Borrows the text of a JSON string without copying it. Accepts a JsonValue owner or JsonView; other JSON kinds return Err with code expected-string and offset zero. Returns Ok(StringView). The source is unchanged.

The view supports length, startsWith, endsWith, includes, indexOf and lastIndexOf. Length and search coordinates use UTF-8 bytes; explicit positions must be scalar boundaries. typeof returns string, Boolean(view) is false only for empty text, and console output displays the text. String(view) makes an independent owned string. Other string operations require that explicit conversion.

```tsrust
import {asString} from "std:json";function main(){const owner=JSON.parse('"hello"');match(asString(owner)){Ok(text)=>{console.log(typeof text,text.length,text.includes("ell"),String(text));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: string 5 true hello.

Ownership: the view may be stored or returned only while its source owner remains alive. The owner cannot be moved or replaced while the view is retained. clone(view) is rejected; use String(view) to copy. An error carries no source loan.

std:json.name: JsonView
std:json.documentation:
A read-only reference to a JSON value owned elsewhere. It cannot be constructed or cloned. typeof, Array.isArray and equality with null inspect its contained data. Scalar readers, kind, stringify, get and at accept the view. Owning extraction with takeString requires JsonValue.

```tsrust
import {get} from "std:json";function main(){const owner=JSON.parse('{"name":"Ada"}');match(get(owner,"name")){Ok(value)=>{if(value!==undefined){console.log(typeof value);}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: string. Ownership: the view retains the original owner lifetime. The owner cannot be moved or replaced while the view is retained. Views may be reborrowed; missing and error branches carry no child loan.

std:json.name: get
std:json.signature: get(value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>, key: ReadOnly<string>): Result<JsonView | undefined, JsonError>

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Required owner or existing read-only JSON view.

parameters.label: key: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Exact UTF-8 object key; empty keys are valid. No coercion or path syntax.

std:json.documentation:
Reads one object child by its exact key. Arrays and scalar values return expected-object. Returns Ok(undefined) when the child is absent, Ok with a borrowed JsonView when present, or Err with JsonError on a wrong container kind. A present JSON null is a view, distinct from undefined. Errors have offset zero because values retain no source position. No mutation or copying occurs.

```tsrust
import {get} from "std:json";function main(){const owner=JSON.parse('{"answer":null}');match(get(owner,"answer")){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value!==undefined,value===null);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: true true. Ownership: the view retains the original owner lifetime. The owner cannot be moved or replaced while the view is retained. Views may be reborrowed; missing and error branches carry no child loan.

std:json.name: at
std:json.signature: at(value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>, index: int): Result<JsonView | undefined, JsonError>

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Required owner or existing read-only JSON view.

parameters.label: index: int
parameters.documentation: Zero-based nonnegative index. Negative indices return index-range; out-of-bounds indices are absent.

std:json.documentation:
Reads one array child. Objects and scalar values return expected-array. Negative indices reject rather than count backward. Returns Ok(undefined) when the child is absent, Ok with a borrowed JsonView when present, or Err with JsonError on a wrong container kind. A present JSON null is a view, distinct from undefined. Errors have offset zero because values retain no source position. No mutation or copying occurs.

```tsrust
import {at} from "std:json";function main(){const owner=JSON.parse("[1]");match(at(owner,1)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value===undefined);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: true. Ownership: the view retains the original owner lifetime. The owner cannot be moved or replaced while the view is retained. Views may be reborrowed; missing and error branches carry no child loan.

std:json.name: asBoolean

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Required JSON value. No coercion or optional arguments.

std:json.documentation:
Reads a JSON boolean without coercion. Other JSON kinds return Err(expected-boolean). Returns Ok with the extracted value or Err with a structured JsonError. Extraction errors use offset zero because JsonValue does not retain source locations.

```tsrust
import {asBoolean} from "std:json"; function main(){match(asBoolean(JSON.parse('false'))){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: false. Ownership: Borrows value without mutation or copying; the scalar result is independent.

std:json.name: asInt

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Required JSON value. No coercion or optional arguments.

std:json.documentation:
Reads an exact signed 64-bit integer. Integral floating values are accepted within [-9223372036854775808, 9223372036854775807]. Fractions return Err(integer-fractional); out-of-range values return Err(integer-range); other JSON kinds return Err(expected-number). Floating negative zero becomes integer zero. Returns Ok with the extracted value or Err with a structured JsonError. Extraction errors use offset zero because JsonValue does not retain source locations.

```tsrust
import {asInt} from "std:json"; function main(){match(asInt(JSON.parse('42.0'))){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: 42. Ownership: Borrows value without mutation or copying; the scalar result is independent.

std:json.name: asNumber

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Required JSON value. No coercion or optional arguments.

std:json.documentation:
Reads a floating-point number. Integer-backed values are accepted only when exactly representable as number; otherwise returns Err(number-precision). Other JSON kinds return Err(expected-number). Preserves stored floating values, including negative zero. Parsing may already round decimals and integers outside the 64-bit range; this operation cannot recover the original spelling. Returns Ok with the extracted value or Err with a structured JsonError. Extraction errors use offset zero because JsonValue does not retain source locations.

```tsrust
import {asNumber} from "std:json"; function main(){match(asNumber(JSON.parse('1.5'))){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: 1.5. Ownership: Borrows value without mutation or copying; the scalar result is independent.

std:json.name: takeString

parameters.label: value: JsonValue
parameters.documentation: Required JSON value. No coercion or optional arguments.

std:json.documentation:
Extracts an owned string from a JSON string without copying its storage. Other JSON kinds return Err(expected-string). The input is consumed on both success and failure. Unicode text is preserved without coercion. Returns Ok with the extracted value or Err with a structured JsonError. Extraction errors use offset zero because JsonValue does not retain source locations.

```tsrust
import {takeString} from "std:json"; function main(){match(takeString(JSON.parse('"hello"'))){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: hello. Ownership: Consumes value; the returned string owns its storage.

std:json.name: JsonValue
std:json.documentation:
An owned strict JSON value: null, boolean, number, string, array or object. Obtain values with parse; inspect their category with kind and encode with stringify. No public fields or direct record construction. Null is a JSON value; undefined is not. Object keys are sorted lexicographically and duplicate keys keep the last value. Signed 64-bit and unsigned 64-bit integers remain exact; other numeric values use finite floating point, including negative zero. Larger integer tokens may round as floating point. Cycles and shared object identity cannot be represented.

```tsrust
import {parse,kind} from "std:json"; function main(){match(parse("null")){Ok(value)=>{console.log(kind(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: null. Ownership: independent owned storage; explicit clone recursively copies the value. No input borrow survives parsing.

std:json.name: JsonError
std:json.signature: type JsonError = { code: string; message: string; offset: int }
std:json.documentation:
Describes a JSON failure without including input values or keys. code distinguishes invalid-json, unexpected-end, trailing-data, invalid-limits, byte-limit, depth-limit, entry-limit, node-limit, output-limit and unterminated-comment. message is fixed explanatory text. offset counts UTF-8 bytes from zero; unexpected-end points to input length. Resource failures point to the parser checkpoint, which may precede the next value. Output failures report bytes written before the rejected output chunk. Invalid limits and scalar extraction failures use zero. Scalar readers also report expected-boolean, expected-number, expected-string, integer-fractional, integer-range and number-precision. Child inspection also reports expected-object, expected-array and index-range. No mutation occurs.

```tsrust
import {parse} from "std:json"; function main(){match(parse("null secret")){Ok(_)=>{throw "unexpected success";},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code,error.offset);}}}
```

Expected output: trailing-data 5. Ownership: ordinary owned record; explicit clone copies it.

std:json.name: JsonLimits
std:json.signature: type JsonLimits = { maxBytes: int; maxDepth: int; maxEntries: int; maxNodes: int }
std:json.documentation:
Sets parse budgets. All four fields are required nonnegative integers. maxBytes bounds UTF-8 input bytes, maxDepth bounds nested containers and cannot exceed 64, maxEntries bounds each array/object including duplicate object entries, and maxNodes bounds total JSON values including containers but excluding object keys. Zero is allowed. Scalars have depth zero. When limits are omitted, defaults are 16777216 bytes, 64 levels, 1000000 entries per collection and 1000000 values. Invalid settings return invalid-limits.

```tsrust
import {parse,JsonLimits} from "std:json"; function main(){const limits:JsonLimits={maxBytes:20,maxDepth:2,maxEntries:1,maxNodes:10};match(parse("[1,2]",limits)){Ok(_)=>{throw "unexpected success";},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code);}}}
```

Expected output: entry-limit. Ownership: parse reads this record without consuming or mutating it.

std:json.name: parse
std:json.signature: parse(text: ReadOnly<string>, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>): Result<JsonValue, JsonError>

parameters.label: text: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Required strict JSON document. UTF-8 byte length is bounded by maxBytes.

parameters.label: limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>
parameters.documentation: Optional complete limits record. Omission uses the documented defaults; negative limits or maxDepth above 64 return invalid-limits.

std:json.documentation:
Parses one strict JSON document and returns Ok with an independent JsonValue or Err with a structured JsonError. text is UTF-8; leading and trailing JSON whitespace is allowed. Trailing non-whitespace, malformed syntax, invalid escapes, lone surrogates and nonfinite numbers reject. Duplicate object keys keep the last value and count toward maxEntries. Keys are sorted, integers within signed/unsigned 64-bit ranges remain exact, larger integers may round to finite floating point, and negative zero survives. Optional limits default to 16777216 bytes, 64 container levels, 1000000 entries per collection and 1000000 values. Budget failures have distinct codes; offset counts bytes, not characters. Neither argument changes.

```tsrust
import {parse,kind} from "std:json"; function main(){match(parse("null")){Ok(value)=>{console.log(kind(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: null. Ownership: borrows both arguments; the result owns all parsed storage and can outlive the input.

Integer tokens without a decimal point or exponent are preserved exactly within signed 64-bit or unsigned 64-bit JSON storage. Tokens outside that storage range are rejected instead of rounded; integer-range reports storage overflow, while invalid or nonfinite JSON can fail earlier. Extracting int still requires the signed 64-bit range. Decimal and exponent forms use floating-point JSON semantics.

std:json.name: kind

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Required JSON value to inspect without mutation.

std:json.documentation:
Returns the JSON category: null, boolean, number, string, array or object. The value argument is required; there are no optional arguments or validation errors. Does not inspect, convert or mutate child values. JSON null reports "null".

```tsrust
import {parse,kind} from "std:json"; function main(){match(parse("null")){Ok(value)=>{console.log(kind(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: null. Ownership: borrows value without consuming it; returns an independent category string.

std:json.name: stringify
std:json.signature: stringify(value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>, maxBytes?: int): Result<string, JsonError>

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<JsonValue | JsonView>
parameters.documentation: Required JSON value. Its contents are not mutated or consumed.

parameters.label: maxBytes?: int
parameters.documentation: Optional output byte limit, default 16777216. Zero rejects every JSON value; negative values return invalid-limits.

std:json.documentation:
Encodes a JsonValue or JsonView as compact strict JSON with sorted object keys and no extra whitespace. Returns Ok with a UTF-8 string or Err(output-limit) before writing beyond maxBytes. The optional nonnegative integer byte limit defaults to 16777216; a negative value returns invalid-limits. Escapes quotes, backslashes and control characters; other Unicode remains UTF-8. Exact integer values are retained and floating negative zero is emitted with its sign. JsonValue cannot contain undefined, nonfinite numbers, cycles or shared object identity. The value is unchanged.

```tsrust
import {parse,stringify} from "std:json"; function main(){match(parse('{"z":1,"a":2}')){Ok(value)=>{match(stringify(value)){Ok(text)=>{console.log(text);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: {"a":2,"z":1}. Ownership: borrows value; the output string owns independent storage.

std:json.name: parseJsonc
std:json.signature: parseJsonc(text: ReadOnly<string>, allowTrailingComma?: boolean, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>): Result<JsonValue, JsonError>
std:json.typedSignature: parseJsonc<T>(text: ReadOnly<string>, allowTrailingComma?: boolean, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>): Result<T, JsonError>

parameters.label: text: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Required UTF-8 JSONC document. Original input bytes, including comments, count against maxBytes.

parameters.label: allowTrailingComma?: boolean
parameters.documentation: Optional, default false. Set true to accept one comma after the final array element or object property.

parameters.label: limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>
parameters.documentation: Optional complete parse budgets, with the same defaults and ranges as parse.

std:json.documentation:
Parses JSON with // line comments and /* block comments */ wherever JSON permits whitespace. Comment delimiters inside strings remain literal. Line comments end at LF or CR; block comments end at the first */ and do not nest. Returns Ok with an owned JsonValue or Err with a JsonError. Unterminated block comments return unterminated-comment at the opening slash. All offsets address original UTF-8 input bytes. Trailing commas reject unless allowTrailingComma is true; empty collections with a comma and repeated commas always reject. Limits default to 16777216 input bytes, 64 container levels, 1000000 entries per collection and 1000000 values. Comment bytes count toward the input limit. Number, Unicode and duplicate-key rules match parse. Comments are discarded; stringify emits strict JSON. Neither argument changes.

```tsrust
import {parseJsonc,kind} from "std:json"; function main(){match(parseJsonc("/* note */ [1,]",true)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(kind(value));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: array. Ownership: borrows text and limits; allocates bounded scratch storage and an independent owned result.

With an explicit type argument, parseJsonc<T> returns Result<T, JsonError> and constructs the owned target directly. Supports scalars, named records, tuples, arrays and nullable records. Required fields must be present; missing optional fields become undefined; unknown fields are skipped but still count against limits. Every duplicate known field must match its type; the last valid occurrence wins. Shape mismatches report shape-mismatch. int conversion is checked; number rejects lossy integer conversion with number-precision. Unsupported targets fail during checking.

```tsrust
import {parseJsonc} from "std:json";type Item={name:string;};function main(){match(parseJsonc<Item>('/*note*/{"name":"hello"}')){Ok(item)=>{console.log(item.name);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}
```

Expected output: hello. Ownership: typed output owns its fields independently of the input and normalization buffer.

Integer tokens without a decimal point or exponent are preserved exactly within signed 64-bit or unsigned 64-bit JSON storage. Tokens outside that storage range are rejected instead of rounded; integer-range reports storage overflow, while invalid or nonfinite JSON can fail earlier. Extracting int still requires the signed 64-bit range. Decimal and exponent forms use floating-point JSON semantics.

std:json.name: JsonlReader
std:json.documentation:
A uniquely owned, bounded JSON Lines file reader. Open with openJsonl, pull one value with readJsonl and consume with closeJsonl. JSON null is distinct from EOF (undefined). No public fields, construction or clone. Owned records survive subsequent reads and reader closure. Scope exit releases the file; explicit close reports close failures.

```tsrust
import {openJsonl,readJsonl,closeJsonl,kind} from "std:json"; import {writeFile} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes";
function main(){match(fromUtf8("null\n")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(writeFile("jsonl-example.jsonl",bytes)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(openJsonl("jsonl-example.jsonl")){Ok(reader)=>{match(readJsonl(reader)){Ok(value)=>{if(value===undefined){throw "unexpected EOF";}console.log(kind(value));},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(closeJsonl(reader)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}
```

Expected output: null.

Ownership: one file owner; reads require mutable access and close consumes the reader.

examples.source:
import {openJsonl,readJsonl,closeJsonl,kind} from "std:json"; import {writeFile} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes";
function main(){match(fromUtf8("null\n")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(writeFile("jsonl-example.jsonl",bytes)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(openJsonl("jsonl-example.jsonl")){Ok(reader)=>{match(readJsonl(reader)){Ok(value)=>{if(value===undefined){throw "unexpected EOF";}console.log(kind(value));},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(closeJsonl(reader)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}

std:json.name: JsonlError
std:json.signature: type JsonlError = { code: string; message: string; operation: string; line: int; offset: int; osCode?: int }
std:json.documentation:
A structured JSON Lines failure. code distinguishes JSON syntax/limit failures, capacity-range and file errors. message never includes record contents or paths. operation is open, read or close. Read line counts records from one and offset is the absolute zero-based UTF-8 byte offset. Open uses line 1 and offset 0; close uses 0 for both because it has no input location. osCode is present only when supplied by the operating system. A read failure is terminal and repeats without further I/O.

```tsrust
import {openJsonl} from "std:json";function main(){match(openJsonl("unused.jsonl",{maxBytes:64,maxDepth:4,maxEntries:8,maxNodes:16},0)){Ok(_)=>{throw "unexpected success";},Err(error)=>{console.log(error.code,error.operation);}}}
```

Expected output: capacity-range open.

Ownership: an independent owned record; explicit clone copies it. Raw fragments preserve their exact text. A literal CR or LF in encoded raw text returns record-newline before any bytes of that record are written and makes the writer terminal. Escaped newline sequences inside JSON strings remain valid; ordinary strings are escaped normally.

code.documentation: Stable failure category, including JSON syntax/limit errors, capacity-range and file errors. Does not contain input.

message.documentation: Fixed explanatory message. Never includes record contents or file paths.

operation.documentation: Operation that failed: open, read or close.

line.documentation: One-based JSON Lines record for read errors. Open errors use 1; close errors use 0 because no input location applies.

offset.documentation: Absolute zero-based UTF-8 input byte offset for read errors. Open and close errors use 0.

osCode.documentation: Optional native operating-system error code. Undefined when the failure has no OS code.

std:json.name: openJsonl
std:json.signature: openJsonl(path: ReadOnly<string>, limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>, capacity?: int): Result<JsonlReader, JsonlError>

parameters.label: path: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Required local file path, borrowed unchanged. Opened read-only; no whole-file load.

parameters.label: limits?: ReadOnly<JsonLimits>
parameters.documentation: Per-record limits; defaults: maxBytes 16777216, maxDepth 64, maxEntries/maxNodes 1000000. Nonnegative; depth at most 64. LF is excluded; CR and other whitespace count.

parameters.label: capacity?: int
parameters.documentation: Read-ahead buffer bytes, 1 through 1048576; defaults to 8192. Invalid capacity or limits reject before opening.

std:json.documentation:
Opens a file for bounded synchronous JSON Lines reading. path is a required local path. Optional limits default to maxBytes 16777216, maxDepth 64, maxEntries/maxNodes 1000000 per record; values must be nonnegative and depth at most 64. LF is excluded from maxBytes, while CR and other whitespace count. Optional capacity defaults to 8192 bytes and must be 1 through 1048576. Optional arguments can be omitted at the end; provide limits when specifying capacity. Validates capacity and limits before opening. Returns an owned reader or a structured open/capacity/limit error. Does not decode a record yet. Each pull retains only one bounded record plus the selected read-ahead buffer. The file is read-only; path is unchanged.

```tsrust
import {openJsonl,readJsonl,closeJsonl,kind} from "std:json"; import {writeFile} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes";
function main(){match(fromUtf8("null\n")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(writeFile("jsonl-example.jsonl",bytes)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(openJsonl("jsonl-example.jsonl")){Ok(reader)=>{match(readJsonl(reader)){Ok(value)=>{if(value===undefined){throw "unexpected EOF";}console.log(kind(value));},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(closeJsonl(reader)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}
```

Expected output: null.

Ownership: the returned reader owns the file and releases it on EOF, read error, early scope exit or consuming close.

import {openJsonl,readJsonl,closeJsonl,kind} from "std:json"; import {writeFile} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes";
function main(){match(fromUtf8("null\n")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(writeFile("jsonl-example.jsonl",bytes)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(openJsonl("jsonl-example.jsonl")){Ok(reader)=>{match(readJsonl(reader)){Ok(value)=>{if(value===undefined){throw "unexpected EOF";}console.log(kind(value));},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(closeJsonl(reader)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}

std:json.name: readJsonl
std:json.typedSignature: readJsonl<T>(reader: Mutable<JsonlReader | JsonlReaderView>): Result<T | undefined, JsonlError>

parameters.label: reader: Mutable<JsonlReader>
parameters.documentation: Required live reader. Advances by one strict JSON record; retained read-ahead stays in the reader. Also accepts a JsonlReaderView; the underlying owner stays exclusively borrowed.

std:json.documentation:
Decodes the next strict JSON value into independent owned storage. Ok(undefined) means EOF; a JSON null is a JsonValue whose kind is null. Accepts LF, CRLF and a final record without LF. Blank lines and BOMs fail. Per-record limits come from openJsonl. Returns an absolute byte offset and record line on error; subsequent reads repeat that terminal error without I/O. EOF and read error release the file; repeated EOF returns undefined. Each successful read advances the reader.

```tsrust
import {openJsonl,readJsonl,closeJsonl,kind} from "std:json"; import {writeFile} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes";
function main(){match(fromUtf8("null\n")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(writeFile("jsonl-example.jsonl",bytes)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(openJsonl("jsonl-example.jsonl")){Ok(reader)=>{match(readJsonl(reader)){Ok(value)=>{if(value===undefined){throw "unexpected EOF";}console.log(kind(value));},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(closeJsonl(reader)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}
```

Expected output: null.

Ownership: mutably borrows the reader during the call. The returned value owns its data and can outlive the reader.

Supply an explicit type argument with readJsonl<T>(reader) to construct T directly. Returns Result<T | undefined, JsonlError>; undefined means EOF and a decoded null remains null. Shape mismatches report shape-mismatch and make the reader terminal. Typed field, numeric and limit rules match JSON.tryParse<T>. Each returned value owns its fields independently of both the reader and later reads.

```tsrust
import {openJsonl,readJsonl,closeJsonl,kind} from "std:json"; import {writeFile} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes";
type Item={name:string;};function main(){match(fromUtf8('{"name":"hello"}\n')){Ok(bytes)=>{match(writeFile("jsonl-example.jsonl",bytes)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(openJsonl("jsonl-example.jsonl")){Ok(reader)=>{match(readJsonl<Item>(reader)){Ok(value)=>{if(value===undefined){throw "unexpected EOF";}console.log(value.name);},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(closeJsonl(reader)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}
```

Also accepts JsonlReaderView from borrowJsonl. Borrowed adapter errors use line/byte offsets relative to adapter creation; closing or dropping it leaves the underlying owner open with unread buffered bytes preserved.

parameters.label: reader: JsonlReader
parameters.documentation: Required owned reader, consumed even if close fails. Cannot be reused afterward. Also accepts JsonlReaderView, releasing its borrow without closing its owner.

std:json.documentation:
Closes a JSON Lines reader early and releases its buffer. Returns Ok on successful close or JsonlError for a close failure. If EOF/error already released the file, close succeeds without closing another descriptor. A prior read error was already returned by readJsonl and is not repeated by close. No implicit sync occurs.


Expected output: null.

std:json.name: JsonlWriter
std:json.documentation:
An opaque owned JSON Lines output resource created by createJsonl. No public constructor or fields. Writes compact records through a bounded staging buffer and a buffered file. flushJsonl reports buffered output failures; closeJsonlWriter consumes the writer and reports cleanup errors. Scope exit closes remaining output but cannot report errors. Ownership: unique, nonclonable and nonconstructible; never shared implicitly.


std:json.name: createJsonl
std:json.signature: createJsonl(path: ReadOnly<string>, maxBytes?: int, capacity?: int): Result<JsonlWriter, JsonlError>

parameters.label: path: ReadOnly<string>
parameters.documentation: Output path. Creates a file or truncates an existing file after validating options.

parameters.label: maxBytes?: int
parameters.documentation: Maximum encoded bytes per record, excluding LF; nonnegative, default 16777216. Zero permits creation but rejects every record.

parameters.label: capacity?: int
parameters.documentation: Output buffer capacity in bytes, from 1 through 1048576; default 8192. Supply maxBytes when specifying capacity.

std:json.documentation:
Creates or truncates a file for bounded synchronous JSON Lines output. Returns an owned writer or a structured error. Invalid maxBytes reports invalid-limits; invalid capacity reports capacity-range before opening or truncating the path. File errors preserve their stable code and optional OS code. Creation errors use operation create, line 1 and offset 0. Record limits exclude the trailing LF. No record is written by creation. Ownership: borrows path unchanged; returned writer owns its file and buffer.

```tsrust

```

std:json.name: writeJsonl
std:json.signature: writeJsonl<T>(writer: Mutable<JsonlWriter>, value: T): Result<void, JsonlError>
std:json.inferredSignature: writeJsonl<T>(writer: Mutable<JsonlWriter | JsonlWriterView>, value: T): Result<void, JsonlError>

parameters.label: writer: Mutable<JsonlWriter>
parameters.documentation: Required writer, advanced on successful record output. Also accepts JsonlWriterView; the underlying owner remains open after adapter close.

parameters.label: value: T
parameters.documentation: Required encodable scalar, record, tuple, array, JsonValue, JsonView or StringView; borrowed unchanged.

std:json.documentation:
Encodes one compact strict JSON record followed by LF. Returns Ok or a structured encoding/output error. Uses JSON.stringify typed rules: sorted keys, exact integers, omitted undefined object fields, undefined-value for root/array undefined, number-nonfinite for nonfinite numbers and depth-limit beyond 64 containers. Stages the entire record within the creation byte limit; output-limit or another encoding rejection writes none of that record. An I/O failure may leave a prefix and has no rollback guarantee. Any error makes subsequent writes/flushes repeat that terminal error without more output. Errors use operation write, the current one-based record and offset 0, which is not an output position. Ownership: mutably borrows writer and borrows value without mutation or implicit cloning.

```tsrust

```

Expected output: hello. The file contains {"name":"hello"} followed by LF.

Also accepts JsonlWriterView from borrowJsonlWriter. The adapter exclusively borrows a BufferedWriter. Closing the adapter flushes its output and leaves the underlying owner open; errors use a record counter starting at adapter creation. Raw fragments preserve their exact text. A literal CR or LF in encoded raw text returns record-newline before any bytes of that record are written and makes the writer terminal. Escaped newline sequences inside JSON strings remain valid; ordinary strings are escaped normally.

std:json.name: flushJsonl

parameters.label: writer: Mutable<JsonlWriter>
parameters.documentation: Required writer; flushes buffered bytes without closing it. Also accepts JsonlWriterView; the underlying owner remains open after adapter close.

std:json.documentation:
Flushes buffered JSON Lines output and reports errors. Does not sync storage for crash durability. Success leaves the writer usable. A failure is terminal; later writes/flushes repeat it. Flush errors use operation flush, offset 0 and the next-record counter; that counter does not identify which buffered record caused failure. A previous terminal error is returned unchanged. Ownership: mutably borrows the writer; does not consume it.

```tsrust

```

Expected output: hello. The file contains {"name":"hello"} followed by LF.

Also accepts JsonlWriterView from borrowJsonlWriter. The adapter exclusively borrows a BufferedWriter. Closing the adapter flushes its output and leaves the underlying owner open; errors use a record counter starting at adapter creation.

std:json.name: closeJsonlWriter

parameters.label: writer: JsonlWriter
parameters.documentation: Required owned writer, consumed even when closing fails. Also accepts JsonlWriterView; the underlying owner remains open after adapter close.

std:json.documentation:
Flushes and closes JSON Lines output, releasing its buffer. Always attempts cleanup after a prior write/flush failure. A close failure takes precedence; otherwise a prior terminal error is returned again. Returns Ok when both writing and closing succeeded. New close errors use operation close, offset 0 and the next-record counter. No implicit storage sync occurs. Ownership: consumes the writer even on error; later use is rejected. Scope exit also attempts close but cannot report errors.

```tsrust

```

Expected output: hello. The file contains {"name":"hello"} followed by LF.

Also accepts JsonlWriterView from borrowJsonlWriter. The adapter exclusively borrows a BufferedWriter. Closing the adapter flushes its output and leaves the underlying owner open; errors use a record counter starting at adapter creation.

std:json.name: JsonlReaderView
std:json.documentation:
Borrows an existing BufferedReader for bounded JSON Lines reading from its current position. Does not reopen, seek or consume a record during construction. Uses the existing read-ahead buffer; no second file buffer is allocated. Optional limits default to maxBytes 16777216, maxDepth 64 and maxEntries/maxNodes 1000000 per record. Limits must be nonnegative and depth at most 64; invalid limits return invalid-limits without reading. LF is excluded from maxBytes; CR and other whitespace count. Returns a JsonlReaderView or JsonlError. readJsonl and readJsonl<T> accept this adapter. Decoded values own their storage. EOF is undefined, distinct from JSON null. Read failures are terminal for this adapter. Error line and byte offset start at 1 and 0 at adapter creation, relative to the starting reader position. closeJsonl or scope exit releases the adapter and preserves unread buffered bytes; neither closes the underlying file.

```tsrust
import {open,bufferReader,close,writeFile} from "std:fs";import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes";import {borrowJsonl,readJsonl,closeJsonl} from "std:json";
function main(){match(fromUtf8("7\n")){Ok(bytes)=>{writeFile("borrowed-jsonl-example.jsonl",bytes);},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}match(open("borrowed-jsonl-example.jsonl")){Ok(file)=>{match(bufferReader(file,8)){Ok(input)=>{{match(borrowJsonl(input)){Ok(reader)=>{match(readJsonl<int>(reader)){Ok(value)=>{if(value!==undefined){console.log(value);}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}closeJsonl(reader);},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}close(input);},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}},Err(e)=>{throw e.message;}}}
```

Expected output: 7.

Ownership: exclusively borrows the buffered reader. The owner cannot be read, moved or closed while the adapter is live. The adapter cannot escape its owner, be cloned or be constructed directly; close the owner explicitly after releasing the adapter.

std:json.name: JsonlWriterView
std:json.documentation:
Borrows an existing BufferedWriter for bounded JSON Lines output at its current position. Does not create, reopen, truncate or seek a file. Uses the existing output buffer. Optional maxBytes defaults to 16777216 and must be nonnegative and fit the platform; it limits each encoded record excluding the final LF. Zero rejects every JSON value. Invalid limits return invalid-limits before writing or flushing. Returns a JsonlWriterView or JsonlError. Existing writeJsonl, flushJsonl and closeJsonlWriter accept the adapter. Typed writes borrow their input and stage a complete bounded record before writing; encoding errors emit no part of that record. I/O errors may leave a prefix. Errors make the adapter terminal. Error line starts at 1 for this adapter; offset is always zero, not a byte position. Closing or dropping the adapter flushes buffered output but leaves the owner open. Explicit close reports a flush error; otherwise it repeats any prior terminal error. Drop cannot report errors. No durability sync is performed.


Expected file contents: 7 followed by LF. No console output.

Ownership: exclusively borrows the buffered writer. The owner cannot be written, flushed, moved or closed while the adapter is live. The view cannot escape its owner, be cloned or be constructed directly. Close the owner explicitly after releasing the adapter.

std:schema.name: s
std:schema.documentation: Imported namespace for constructing reusable validation schemas. Import aliases preserve its identity. string() and boolean() construct scalar schemas; safeParse validates matching scalar values or owned JSON input. Importing the namespace alone adds no runtime dependency. Ownership: the namespace itself owns no runtime value.

std:schema.name: Schema
std:schema.documentation: Opaque schema with inferred output type T. Construct through the imported s builders. A Schema<string> cannot be assigned to Schema<int>. It cannot be constructed as a record, inspected as data or implicitly copied. Scalar safeParse returns a typed Result.

std:schema.name: SchemaError
std:schema.documentation: Validation failure containing issues and a truncated flag. Issues contain controlled type summaries and paths; input values are never retained. Current string validation emits one root issue on mismatch. Ownership: the error owns its issue collection.

std:schema.name: SchemaIssue
std:schema.documentation: One validation issue: code, path, pathTruncated, expected and observed. The root path is empty. expected and observed describe types rather than input contents. Ownership: owns its strings and path.

std:schema.name: SchemaPath
std:schema.documentation: One path segment. A field segment has field set and index absent; an array segment has index set and field absent. Indices are zero-based. Root issues have no segments. Ownership: owns any field name.

std:schema.name: SchemaConstructionError
std:schema.signature: type SchemaConstructionError = { code: string; operation: string; limit: int | number }
std:schema.documentation: Thrown when constructing invalid schema bounds. code is negative-length for string limits, nonfinite-limit for floating limits, or contradictory-bounds; operation identifies min, max, gt or lt; limit retains the supplied int or number without converting exact integers to floating point. Narrow the limit before arithmetic. This error concerns schema construction, not input validation through safeParse. Contains no input data.

schemaBuilder.name: string
schemaBuilder.documentation:
Constructs a reusable schema whose output type is string. Takes no arguments and does not validate input by itself. The constructor has no constraints or receiver mutation; passing any argument is an error. Use safeParse to validate owned string or JSON input. Chain min and max to constrain Unicode code-point length.

```tsrust
import {s, Schema} from 'std:schema'; function make():Schema<string>{return s.string();} function main(){const value=make(); console.log('schema created');}
```

Expected output: schema created.

Ownership: returns an owned immutable schema value; no source text is borrowed.

examples.source: import {s, Schema} from 'std:schema'; function make():Schema<string>{return s.string();} function main(){const value=make(); console.log('schema created');}

schemaBuilder.name: boolean
schemaBuilder.documentation:
Constructs a reusable boolean schema. Takes no arguments, performs no coercion and does not mutate the namespace. safeParse accepts concrete booleans or owned JsonValue input. False is a valid value, not a validation failure.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.boolean();match(schema.safeParse(false)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value);},Err(error)=>{throw 'unexpected';}}}
```

Expected output: false.

Ownership: returns an owned immutable schema; no input storage is borrowed.

schemaBuilder.name: int
schemaBuilder.documentation:
Constructs a reusable signed 64-bit integer schema. Takes no arguments and does not mutate the namespace. safeParse accepts a concrete int or owned JsonValue. Numeric JSON must be integral and within -9223372036854775808 through 9223372036854775807. Strings and booleans are not coerced.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.int();match(schema.safeParse(42)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value);},Err(error)=>{throw 'unexpected';}}}
```

Expected output: 42.

Ownership: returns an owned immutable schema; no input is borrowed.

schemaBuilder.name: number
schemaBuilder.documentation:
Constructs a reusable finite floating-point number schema. Takes no arguments and does not mutate the namespace. safeParse accepts a concrete number, int or owned JsonValue. Exact JSON integers must be representable as number without precision loss. NaN and infinities are rejected. Use s.int() when exact signed 64-bit integer output is required.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){const schema=s.number();match(schema.safeParse(1.5)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value);},Err(error)=>{throw 'unexpected';}}}
```

Expected output: 1.5.

Ownership: returns an owned immutable schema; no input storage is borrowed.

schemaBuilder.name: null
schemaBuilder.documentation:
Constructs a reusable schema accepting only null. Takes no arguments, performs no coercion and does not mutate the namespace. Null is a present value, distinct from undefined or a missing field.

```tsrust
import {s} from 'std:schema';function main(){match(s.null().safeParse(null)){Ok(value)=>{console.log(value);},Err(error)=>{throw 'unexpected';}}}
```

Expected output: null.

Ownership: returns an owned immutable schema.

schemaBuilder.name: array

parameters.label: element: Owned<Schema<T>>
parameters.documentation: One element schema, consumed into the array plan. Nested array plans are supported.

schemaBuilder.documentation:
Constructs an immutable array schema that owns its element plan. Existing element constraints are retained without cloning. Returns Schema<T[]>; nesting produces nested array output types. safeParse validates owned matching arrays or JsonValue, including nested arrays. Construction requires exactly one schema and has no optional arguments.

```tsrust
import {s,Schema} from 'std:schema';function main(){const rows:Schema<string[][]> = s.array(s.array(s.string().min(1)));console.log('constructed');}
```

SchemaArray.name: safeParse

parameters.label: input: Owned<Input>
parameters.documentation: A matching owned array or dynamic JSON value. Both transfer on success and failure. JSON arrays are checked recursively without coercing strings, booleans or null. Number schemas also accept int arrays with matching nesting; every integer must convert exactly.

SchemaNumber.name: lt

parameters.label: limit: number
parameters.documentation: Finite floating-point exclusive upper limit. No default. NaN and infinities throw nonfinite-limit.

SchemaNumber.documentation:

NaN or infinite limits throw SchemaConstructionError with code nonfinite-limit; intervals with no finite representable value throw contradictory-bounds. The error records operation lt and the original limit in its int | number field. Validation returns too-small or too-large for bound violations; checked conversion failures retain priority. Exclusive bounds reject the endpoint without an arbitrary epsilon. Positive and negative zero compare equally; successful values retain their sign.

SchemaObject.name: safeParse

parameters.label: input: Owned<Input>
parameters.documentation: An owned matching record or JsonValue. Input transfers on success and failure.

SchemaObject.documentation:


SchemaObject.name: retain
SchemaObject.signature: retain(): Schema<{ value: Output; extra: Map<string, JsonValue> }>
SchemaObject.documentation:
